alternative: Use the JVM GC for memory and bracket the owned resources: scala.util.Using (apply/Manager/resource) releases in reverse acquisition order and combines failures, cats-effect Resource or ZIO Scope brackets acquisition in effectful code, and java.lang.ref types cover weakly held caches - a hand-written owner wrapper cannot control JVM reclamation.
idiom_name: none - JVM reachability owns memory; scala.util.Using / effect-system Resource at the resource edge
implementation_notes: Scala compiles to the JVM, where reachability decides reclamation, so an owning wrapper cannot enforce a heap object's death; what replaces the classic structure is resource bracketing. scala.util.Using wraps acquire/use/release in Try (or rethrows with Using.resource), releases resources in reverse order of creation, and combines a body failure with a release failure by documented severity rules; Using.Manager manages several resources and still releases those acquired before a construction failure. Effect systems model the same bracket inside a program: cats-effect Resource and ZIO Scope acquire and release around a use, with ownership scoped to the effect rather than the object. Non-owning edges use java.lang.ref (WeakReference/WeakHashMap) or a cache built on it.
pitfalls: Using wraps the result in Try by default while Using.resource rethrows: pick the form the call site can handle, and note that release failures are suppressed onto the primary exception rather than dropped.

Using.Manager needs an implicit Manager for self-registering resources; the documented pattern registers on construction precisely so a failure during construction still releases earlier acquisitions.

cats-effect Resource and ZIO Scope require a runtime and only bracket effects - they do not manage plain JVM heap objects, and finalizers run through the effect interpreter, not at ordinary scope exit.
java.lang.ref caches must not assume prompt clearing: ReferenceQueue processing is the application's job, and an entry that stays reachable is never cleared.
